question: A healthy couple has an 8-year-old daughter with hepatosplenomegaly. The laboratory of biochemical genetics has detected in it a deficiency of the acid beta-glucosidase enzyme (glucocerebrosidase) and molecularly presents the mutation N370S in homozygosis. Which diagnosis is correct?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Deficiency of acid beta-glucosidase enzyme (glucocerebrosidase)" -> "Mutation N370S in homozygosis" -> "Gaucher disease" -> 95% CHAIN: "Hepatosplenomegaly" -> "Deficiency of acid beta-glucosidase enzyme (glucocerebrosidase)" -> "Gaucher disease" -> 95%
analysis: The correct diagnosis based on the presented information of hepatosplenomegaly, deficiency of acid beta-glucosidase enzyme, and the mutation N370S in homozygosis is Gaucher disease (1q22). Gaucher disease is an autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by mutations in the GBA gene, leading to the accumulation of glucocerebroside in cells.
